The manipulation of time in the story is exceptionally well-balanced and serves the emotional arc of the narrative. The author uses **compression** effectively to cover the progression of the dream from February to August, as well as to summarize years of Daniel's past marriage to Rachel and his teenage summers with his father in just a few paragraphs. This provides necessary emotional context without bogging down the story. Conversely, the story slows down into real-time or **stretched** moments during pivotal scenes—such as the Sunday morning conversation with Isabel, the twenty minutes Daniel spends looking through his old box of belongings, and the quiet morning on the river in June. This contrast allows the reader to linger in the moments of emotional breakthrough and connection while moving briskly through the passage of the months.
